title: I kept the generated score for my garden RTS and replaced all eight gameplay sounds
author: Public-Influence1587
selftext:
I’m making Dropfolk, a little browser RTS in Godot. Suno gave me a track called Dewdrop Greeting that felt right for the garden. I tried generating the interface and battle effects with ElevenLabs as well. After two rounds, the click was the only one I wanted to keep auditioning.



What helped was a listening page I built with Codex. I could play the actual score, turn it down independently, then try three sounds for each event without touching the game build. For capturing and losing a house I picked the same plucked instrument moving in opposite directions. For the thornflower I picked a single release from a real longbow recording. Even the original click lost to a short Kenney button sound in that comparison.



The new mix is playable here: [https://playgama.ai/play/gkwom4fc6zbzkb](https://playgama.ai/play/gkwom4fc6zbzkb)



If you’ve mixed generated music with library effects, what did you use to decide whether an effect still reads during a busy match?
